question.text: A point charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is placed at origin. Another point charge <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math> is placed at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. Charge of proton is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></math>. The proton is placed on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis so that the electrostatic force on the proton in zero. In this situation, the position of the proton from the origin is ______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Let at point P net electric field is zero.

As direction of electric field due to both charges at point P is opposite, equating magnitude we get

14πε04q0x2=14πε0q0x-122⇒2x-12=x⇒x=24 cm

Distance of proton from origin =24 cm.
